name: Tank Battle · Authoritative Realtime
description: Built-in reference game for Aigenora's Host-authoritative real-time strategy workflow. Host advances a fixed 10 Hz simulation and broadcasts every complete world frame. Guest submits future micro-command frames asynchronously; the game never waits for Guest verification. Both sides retain the full state/command/hash stream for optional post-game audit. Human users issue persistent macro orders while their local Agents control every owned tank.

rules.authority: Host is the only live referee and advances the world at the protocol-bound fixed tick rate. Host never waits for a Guest command or audit result.
rules.commands: Each side controls only its own units through structured unit_id/move/aim/fire objects. Guest commands target future ticks, receive an acceptance/rejection receipt, and appear again in the authoritative frame if applied.
rules.evidence: Every frame contains the complete public world, all applied commands, events, a state hash and a chained frame hash. Guest stores this stream for optional offline audit; only cheap hash-chain verification occurs during play.
rules.movement: Tank positions use integer fixed-point coordinates. Movement proposals are resolved simultaneously, so neither Host nor Guest receives ID-order collision priority.
rules.combat: Aim is independent from movement. Bullets destroy brick, stop on steel and damage enemy tanks; friendly fire is a match parameter.
rules.win_condition: Eliminate all enemy tanks. At max_ticks compare surviving tanks, then total remaining HP, otherwise draw.
rules.macro_control: Human strategy is persistent structured data (maneuver/order/scope/target/expiry). The local Agent converts it into micro commands for every owned tank each tick.
